transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Olivia Torres (Redwood Solutions), Sarah Müller (MediVault CISO), Jonas Becker (MediVault Head of Infra), Elena Garcia (MediVault Legal), Marco Rossi (MediVault Platform)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be imperfect)
- High level: discussion about region pinning and data residency, EU-only requirement for certain datasets, KMS/BYOK, audit logs and sub-processors

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:07] Sarah: Hi, Sarah Müller, CISO at MediVault. We're mainly here to validate EU-only processing for some of our PHI-adjacent workloads.
[00:13] Jonas: Jonas Becker, infra. We'll want a tech deep dive on region pinning and backups.
[00:18] Elena: Elena Garcia from legal — will focus on DPA, SCCs, and sub-processor list.
[00:23] Maya: Great, and Liam's our SE, he'll run the technical details. Liam?
[00:27] Liam: Hey all. Quick agenda — cover hosted vs dedicated vs private, how region pinning works today, KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed), audit logging and retention, sub-processor disclosures and failover behavior.
[00:39] Marco: One quick thing — timeline, we plan to go to pilot next quarter so need answers in the next two weeks ideally.
[00:46] Liam: Sounds good. Starting with architecture: Redwood hosts in multiple regions, EU regions are GCP-europe-west and AWS-eu-central etc, we allow tenant-scoped region pinning for hosted customers — that means requests and storage are routed to the pinned region and we avoid cross-border processing in normal operation.
[01:05] Sarah: "Tenant-scoped" meaning all data including logs and backups stay in the EU?
[01:10] Liam: By default yes — primary storage, model inference and KV cache are in-region. Backups and replica snapshots follow region pinning too; we can configure backup retention and ensure snapshots remain in the same region. Note: some metadata and control-plane signals go to Redwood's control plane which is multi-region — but we do not store customer payload in the control plane.
[01:33] Jonas: That control plane comment — do you ever process tokens or payloads in the control plane for routing or telemetry? We need assurance there's no de-serializing or content-level inspection outside EU.
[01:44] Liam: Good question. The control plane only receives pointers and routing metadata, not message payloads. For hosted we've instrumented telemetry that is privacy-aware; payloads remain in region boundaries. I will caveat: there are rare operational tools that could access metadata; we document those and can restrict via RBAC and JIT audits.
[02:05] Elena: From legal, we need the DPA and SCCs. Also list of sub-processors — including cloud providers and any third-party logging/monitoring vendors.
[02:13] Maya: We'll send the current DPA draft with SCCs and the sub-processor list. We also publish a change-notice cadence for sub-processor additions.
[02:20] Sarah: What about cross-border processing for model providers or inference fallbacks — e.g., if you fall back to a different model in a different region during pressure, does that cross borders?
[02:30] Liam: We have routing policies — by default a pinned tenant will fallback to compatible model variants inside the same region. Cross-region fallback is opt-in; we can configure strict region-only policies that prevent cross-border execution even if capacity is constrained. The tradeoff is potential increased latency or queued requests if the local pool is saturated.
[02:55] Marco: So strict region-only could cause throttling under peak loads?
[02:59] Liam: Exactly, or we'd need to bring dedicated capacity. That's where Redwood Dedicated or Private comes in — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in the chosen region, Private gives you customer VPC or on-prem where we don't touch customer network.
[03:12] Sarah: For compliance we prefer EU-only even if there is a cost.
[03:16] Marco: Can that be done for the hosted product or do we need Dedicated?
[03:20] Liam: Hosted can be EU-only per-tenant with region pinning and strict policy settings. For stronger guarantees (no routing metadata leaving customer VPC, customer-managed peering, or on-prem keys) Dedicated or Private is recommended. Hosted with BYOK is limited — we offer BYOK for Dedicated and Private today; for hosted we support customer-managed KMS in certain enterprise agreements — I will confirm exact coverage.
[03:45] Jonas: Can you explain BYOK behavior — where are keys stored and how are they used for disk encryption vs token encryption?
[03:52] Liam: Sure — with customer-managed KMS (BYOK), you provide the key in your cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS or GCP KMS). We use envelope encryption: data keys are generated per-tenant and encrypted with the customer key. The encrypted data keys and ciphertext stay in your region. For Private deployments you can integrate with your HSM and we never have access to the unwrapped keys. For hosted, the keys are in your KMS and Redwood only receives wrapped keys when needed for ephemeral operations; in practice that means Redwood cannot decrypt data without an active KMS operation in your project.
[04:28] Sarah: Is HSM / FIPS mode supported? We have FIPS requirements for certain data classes.
[04:33] Liam: Private supports full HSM integration and FIPS-certified modules. For Dedicated we can enable KMS-backed HSM options depending on cloud provider. For hosted, we rely on cloud KMS FIPS modes; I'll add specifics to the artifact we send.
[04:46] Elena: Retention of audit logs — legal needs logs for 7 years for some records. What's the retention capability?
[04:53] Liam: Audit logs are configurable — default retention is 90 days in the console, but we support export to customer-managed storage for long-term retention. For enterprise customers we can set longer retention and export options; we can also stream logs to your SIEM (S3, BigQuery, Splunk) so you control lifecycle.
[05:10] Jonas: Are logs stored in the pinned region as well? Backups?
[05:14] Liam: Yes — when region pinned we store logs in-region. Exports to external storage follow your destination—if you export to an EU S3 bucket they'll remain in EU. One caveat: control-plane operational alerts go to multi-region monitoring but payloads and PII are excluded.
[05:29] Sarah: How about metadata — user IDs, model usage metrics — is that considered personal data? We need to know what is in telemetry.
[05:35] Liam: Telemetry is aggregated; raw payloads aren't included. User identifiers and route IDs may be present — we can pseudonymize or hash identifiers. We'll include a telemetry schema in the artifacts.
[05:47] Marco: Sub-processors — do you use any external ops vendors that could access customer data?
[05:52] Maya: We use cloud providers and a small set of monitoring and observability partners; full sub-processor list will be in the doc. We notify customers ahead of material changes.
[05:59] Elena: Is there a breach notification SLA?
[06:02] Maya: Yes, standard incident notification commitments are in the DPA and SOC2 — we'll send the relevant clauses.
[06:08] Sarah: On the topic of EU adequacy — do you rely on SCCs or do you have EU entity processing?
[06:13] Liam: We have an EU legal entity for data processing in some products, but the primary approach for cross-border is SCCs and DPA. For customers requiring an EU-only legal entity, Private deployments or Dedicated contracted in the EU can be scoped under our EU entity; we'll confirm specifics in the DPA.
[06:32] Jonas: What about backups — are snapshot replicas ever replicated outside region for disaster recovery?
[06:38] Liam: By default backups follow region pinning, but for cross-region DR we do offer options — cross-region replication is an opt-in; it's disabled for strict region-only policies. If you want cross-region DR with EU-to-US failover we'd document that and require customer sign-off.
[06:56] Marco: If we pick strict pinned mode and there's an availability event, what would be the RTO?
[07:01] Liam: RTO depends on capacity. If you run on Hosted strict-pin with no dedicated reserve, RTO could be minutes to hours depending on reprovisioning and queued requests. With Dedicated in-region reserved capacity we guarantee lower RTOs per SLA. Private on-prem gives you full control of RTO. We'll include SLO numbers in the tech doc.
[07:22] Sarah: One more on encryption — at-rest and in-transit, are there separate keys per-tenant?
[07:28] Liam: Yes — data keys are tenant-scoped and rotated. In-transit uses TLS with modern ciphers; at-rest uses envelope encryption with tenant data keys backed by customer or Redwood KMS depending on the plan.
[07:41] Elena: Can Redwood provide redaction or deletion proof for GDPR requests?
[07:46] Liam: We support data deletion endpoints and can provide logs showing deletion operations. For immutable backups we document retention windows; upon deletion we can rotate keys or delete data keys to render data unrecoverable in extreme cases — we'll explain options in the DPA.
[08:05] Jonas: About audit logs — can we get raw event streams, e.g., every inference request metadata (timestamp, route, model id, token counts) pushed to our SIEM?
[08:15] Liam: Yes, we can stream structured event logs (no raw payload) to your SIEM. We can include token counts and model ids, but we strip or pseudonymize any user-level PII by default unless you request otherwise.
[08:29] Sarah: A practical ask — can you show a config example that pins a tenant to eu-central and forbids cross-region fallback?
[08:36] Liam: Sure, Liam: "tenant.config.region_pin = eu-central; tenant.config.fallback_policy = region-only;" — I'll include real config samples in the doc and a JSON snippet for the API.
[08:49] Marco: Any limitations on model catalog for EU-only tenants? Some newer models are only in certain regions due to licensing.
[08:56] Liam: Correct — some third-party model variants may be region-limited. For EU-only we supply a curated model catalog certified for EU processing; if you require a specific model we can onboard it under enterprise terms or run it in Dedicated.
[09:10] Elena: On sub-processors again — how do you notify customers of changes? Contractual 30-day notice?
[09:16] Maya: We provide 30 days notice for material changes and update the sub-processor page; critical security patches or emergency changes are communicated faster with rationales.
[09:25] Sarah: Do you have a SOC 2 report we can share with our auditors?
[09:29] Maya: Yes, we'll provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert links under NDA if required.
[09:33] Jonas: For the hosted BYOK caveat — you said limited. Can you follow up with exactly which hosted plans support BYOK and the supportability matrix?
[09:42] Liam: Absolutely. I'll attach the matrix: Hosted (standard) — Redwood-managed keys; Hosted (Enterprise) — BYOK with limitations; Dedicated/Private — BYOK fully supported. I'll confirm exact cloud-provider caveats.
[09:55] Marco: One operational question — who can access keys and logs internally? We need role-based constraints.
[09:59] Liam: We have RBAC and least-privilege operator roles; access to keys is logged and requires dual-approval for certain actions. We'll provide an access matrix and a list of who has privileged access on Redwood side.
[10:11] Elena: Any certifications around people/ops? Background checks?
[10:15] Maya: We can share high-level info in the SOC2 report and supply an employee security policy summary.
[10:22] Sarah: Let's talk about breach SLA again — what's the notification window?
[10:26] Maya: We aim to notify customers within 72 hours for incidents that meet breach definition; for high-severity incidents we target <24 hours initial notification and continuous updates. It's in the DPA.
[10:38] Marco: For our pilot can we start hosted EU-only with strict pin and enable Dedicated if we need headroom?
[10:45] Liam: Yes — that's a common path. Start hosted with region pinning and then move to Dedicated or Private as load or compliance requires. Migration steps are documented; we'll include a migration checklist.
[10:58] Sarah: One more — do you publish a public list of sub-processors currently used in EU region?
[11:03] Maya: Yes, we have a public sub-processor list and will attach region-specific details.
[11:08] Elena: Legal will need the draft DPA and SCCs to start our review — can you get that to us by next Tuesday?
[11:13] Maya: Yes, we'll prioritize that.
[11:15] Liam: I'll follow up with the technical artifacts: region pin config samples, BYOK matrix, audit log export examples, and SLOs for RTO/RPO.
[11:26] Sarah: Thanks. Any final concerns?
[11:29] Marco: None from infra; just need the artifacts and a demo.
[11:33] Elena: We'll await the DPA and sub-processor list.
[11:36] Maya: Great — recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO links, DPA draft with SCCs, sub-processor list, region pin architecture doc, config snippets, BYOK support matrix, and schedule a Private walkthrough with Marco and Jonas.
[11:52] Sarah: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:55] Maya: Thanks, bye.

End of meeting.
